page.title: Functional programming
page.desc: Programs as compositions of functions: first-class functions, immutability and pure functions, rooted in Alonzo Church's lambda calculus of the 1930s.
page.intro: Programs as compositions of functions: first-class functions, immutability and pure functions, rooted in Alonzo Church's lambda calculus of the 1930s.

synapses.text: Church's calculus of function abstraction and application (1930s) is Turing-complete and the theoretical basis of functional languages.

synapses.lead: Pure functions are easy to test
synapses.text: Same inputs, same output, no side effects: pure functions can be tested, memoised and parallelised without ceremony.
map/filter/reduce, lambdas and immutable collections are in Python, JavaScript, Java, Rust and C#; FP won by diffusion.

children.title: Immutability
children.desc: Values that never change after creation; updates produce new values. Removes whole classes of bugs and makes sharing across threads safe.

children.title: Higher-order functions
children.desc: Functions that take or return functions: map, filter, reduce, compose, and the decorators and middleware built from them.
